To: board:vendor-reviews
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Harbor Point Steno Service - Stenvale Aria 3 recalibration and battery

I told Dana on the general board that I would write this up once my machine had been through a real trial. It has now survived eight days of a civil trial, so here is the review.

Equipment: Stenvale Aria 3, serial ending 0388.

Work done: full keyboard recalibration, number bar depression sensor replacement, internal cleaning, firmware update from 4.0.7 to 4.2.1, and replacement of the internal battery. The battery was not part of the original estimate. Gloria emailed on 10/22 to say it was holding about 60% of rated capacity and would be $25 in parts and labor, and she did not proceed until I approved it. I appreciated that.

Dates: dropped off Monday, October 19. Picked up Tuesday, October 27. That is six business days against the ten business days quoted.

Quote and payment: quoted $285. Final invoice $310, including the $25 battery. I paid by card at pickup. I paid personally, as I do for all my equipment; there was no reimbursement from the court.

Loaner: yes, a Stenvale Aria 2 was offered and I took it. It handled the basics. The tilt arm would not hold its position; it slipped mid-afternoon during a deposition and I propped it on a legal pad for the rest of the day. I mentioned it to Gloria so they would know before it went out again, and she said they would repair it.

Performance: my first full day back was expert testimony, an engineer who talks in numbers. The number bar did not double a single stroke. That was the thing I was most worried about, and it held. The machine also came back with a printed one-page service sheet listing every adjustment they made. I have never had that from anyone. It is a small thing, but it tells you they keep a record and want you to have it.

Phone: this is the real weakness. Their phone line is staffed Tuesday through Thursday, 9 to 4 only. I called Wednesday, October 21, to ask about progress. It rang out and there was no voicemail box set up. Gloria emailed me the following day, so the information reached me, but if you are working a Monday docket and something goes sideways over a weekend, that schedule is not much help. I would plan around it: use email, and do not count on reaching a person on a Monday or Friday.

Shop: Harbor Point is a two-person shop off York Road. Parking in the back is free, which sounds trivial until you are carrying a steno machine through a parking garage.

Bottom line for Dana: yes, I would trust them with your Aria. The work was careful, the price was fair for what was done, and they asked before adding the battery, which matters to me. Just go in knowing the phone hours are limited and get everything in email. I would use them again, and I would drop off on a Monday again if it meant getting the machine back in six business days.
